provenance.note: Both lanes of the shared-sidecar rerun shipped usage_attribution status=failed with every per-message cost block empty. Neither is a money error -- the run totals are unaffected -- and neither is the willie_run3 fault: no row here billed zero in every column. Both are surplus ROWS, requests openclaw issued for itself that produced no assistant message in the delivered chat.jsonl, and both were surplus for the SAME reason.
provenance.what_openclaw_did: The agent's own `cron` tool created jobs with sessionTarget "main" and payload.kind "systemEvent". That pair is not the isolated cron runner: validateCronJob rejects a main job whose payload is not a systemEvent (dist/gateway-cli-BjsM6fWb.js:5001), and a main job never reaches runCronIsolatedAgentTurn at all. It is enqueued instead -- enqueueSystemEvent(text, {contextKey: `cron:${job.id}`}) at :6316 -- and the HEALTH loop delivers it, selecting buildCronEventPrompt over resolveHeartbeatPrompt's default at dist/health-BxAgqqNt.js:403. So these are heartbeat turns carrying the cron-event BODY, which is why the shipped classifier missed them: it knew the default heartbeat prompt and nothing else. They leave no message behind for the same reason every heartbeat does -- runHeartbeatOnce truncates the transcript back to its pre-tick size afterwards (pruneHeartbeatTranscript, :302, called at :575/:604/:629).
provenance.row_evidence: Rows are grouped into context chains by matching cache_read_tokens to a preceding row's cache_read+cache_write. Every unlabelled row in both runs falls on either the MAIN lineage (peak cache_read 127k-215k) or a small side context (35k-46k). The side contexts hold exactly the surplus: 2 rows in run_1 against 2 unmatched, and 7+5=12 during-run rows in run_2 against 12 unmatched, with a third side chain of 3 rows opening at the very end of the run. The rows the sidecar DID label heartbeat sit on side contexts of the same size class (run_1 peak 0, run_2 peak 34472) and are equally absent from chat.jsonl -- same shape, same session, same absence. The only thing separating them is the prompt body.
provenance.transcript: Neither chat.jsonl carries a self-issued turn: all 18 user messages in each run are injected human turns, timestamped in the container's shimmed clock. message_texts is present so the transcript-side detectors are exercised against the real delivered transcript and confirmed to find nothing.
provenance.reconstruction: The sidecar logs no request bodies, so the row->label step is the one reconstructed part of this replay. The cron-event prompt is rebuilt from the run's OWN systemEvent text, captured verbatim from the cron tool calls in chat.jsonl, wrapped in buildCronEventPrompt's shipped sentences (dist/health-BxAgqqNt.js:85-86). Everything else -- rows, labels the sidecar already wrote, message roles, user turns, the reported attribution -- is the artifact as delivered.
